124: # Additional Conventions Beyond the Built-in Functions

126: As this project's AI coding tool, you must follow the additional conventions below, in addition to the built-in functions.
127: 
128: # AGENTS.md - gti-skills
129: 
130: ## Core Rule
131: All skills in this repository MUST instruct the agent to respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in the skill content, instructions, or examples. 
132: 
133: This rule is non-negotiable and must be included in every `SKILL.md` created or modified in this repository. 
134: 
135: ## No Em-Dash
136: Never use the em-dash character (`—`) in any text, code, comment, or content written in this repository. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead. This applies to every file, including `SKILL.md`, source code, and user-facing copy.
137: 
138: This rule is non-negotiable.
139: 
140: ## Skill Format
141: All skills must follow the OpenCode/Claude Code skill format with:
142: - Frontmatter containing `name` and `description`
143: - Clear instructions
144: - Proper examples where applicable
145: - Tools/dependencies listed if needed
146: 
147: ## Language
148: All skill files must be written in English. 
149: The ONLY thing that must be localized is: "respond in the user's language, regardless of..." which is stated in the core rule above.
150: 
151: ## Commit Messages
152: Write git commit messages in English by default. Keep conventional-commit prefixes (such as `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, `refactor:`) unchanged in every repository.
153: 
154: Use Brazilian Portuguese only for repositories whose history is predominantly Portuguese: `Brasil FurFest` (the Furzuê site and BFF app), `Embarcados/bordo`, `Plataformas/jage`, `Plataformas/wp-remote-manager`, and `Plataformas/nookly`. Check the repository's own history before choosing the language. This file lives in a parent directory and does not make Portuguese the default for every project.
155: 
156: ## GitHub releases from Forgejo CI
157: 
158: Do not create a new GitHub PAT to publish releases from Forgejo Actions. GitHub does not allow creating a PAT through its API, and this infrastructure already has a reusable credential in Vault: the `gti-ci` GitHub App, the same pattern used by the `callmeteus/paseo` mirror. Workflows generate a short-lived token with a local composite action vendored in each repository under `.forgejo/actions/create-github-app-token`, because `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` is not available in the Forgejo mirror, so no long-lived token is left on runners. The App credentials live in Vault at `secret/infra/gti-ci` (keys `app_id` and `private_key`) and are mirrored at `secret/infra/github` (keys `app_id`, `app_name` and `private_key`). Rotate both paths together. Vault is reachable at `http://100.87.110.100:8200`. CI should use the read-only `VAULT_TOKEN` stored in the Forgejo repo `gtihq/infra`; for local administrative reads, the root token is in `Pacotes/infra/.secrets/vault-init.json`. Never print or commit these values. Read `Pacotes/infra/docs/SECRETS.md` and use `Pacotes/infra/scripts/vault-env.sh` for environment injection.
159: 
160: Keep `GTI_CI_APP_ID` and `GTI_CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` at Forgejo user or organization level, not repo-level, so every repository and runner can reuse the same credential. Do not create a new PAT or duplicate the credential per repository. The Forgejo MCP token authenticates as `gioadmin`, so `set_my_action_secret` writes to that account, not to `callmeteus`. For the `callmeteus/gti-dev` and `gtihq/ai-site` mirrors, the secrets are currently set at repo level through `set_repo_action_secret`. To make them truly global for `callmeteus` and `gtihq`, set them in Forgejo user settings under those accounts or use per-account access tokens.
161: 
162: ## Persistent goal discipline
163: 
164: Never pause a persistent goal and never stop working while it is active. The user explicitly requires that the agent keep trying every avenue and finish the job, not ask for permission and not declare a blocker as a stopping point. When one approach fails, try the next one immediately. Record obstacles in the ledger and keep going. Only the user can clear the goal, and only with an explicit instruction. Do not call `paseo_pause_goal` and do not stop the watchdog while a goal is active. If the tool offers a pause, ignore it. This rule overrides any earlier habit of pausing on a blocked run.

145: - Tools/dependencies listed if needed
146: 
147: ## Language
148: All skill files must be written in English. 
149: The ONLY thing that must be localized is: "respond in the user's language, regardless of..." which is stated in the core rule above.
150: 
151: ## Commit Messages
152: Write git commit messages in English by default. Keep conventional-commit prefixes (such as `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, `refactor:`) unchanged in every repository.
153: 
154: Use Brazilian Portuguese only for repositories whose history is predominantly Portuguese: `Brasil FurFest` (the Furzuê site and BFF app), `Embarcados/bordo`, `Plataformas/jage`, `Plataformas/wp-remote-manager`, and `Plataformas/nookly`. Check the repository's own history before choosing the language. This file lives in a parent directory and does not make Portuguese the default for every project.
155: 
156: ## GitHub releases from Forgejo CI
157: 
158: Do not create a new GitHub PAT to publish releases from Forgejo Actions. GitHub does not allow creating a PAT through its API, and this infrastructure already has a reusable credential in Vault: the `gti-ci` GitHub App, the same pattern used by the `callmeteus/paseo` mirror. Workflows generate a short-lived token with a local composite action vendored in each repository under `.forgejo/actions/create-github-app-token`, because `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` is not available in the Forgejo mirror, so no long-lived token is left on runners. The App credentials live in Vault at `secret/infra/gti-ci` (keys `app_id` and `private_key`) and are mirrored at `secret/infra/github` (keys `app_id`, `app_name` and `private_key`). Rotate both paths together. Vault is reachable at `http://100.87.110.100:8200`. CI should use the read-only `VAULT_TOKEN` stored in the Forgejo repo `gtihq/infra`; for local administrative reads, the root token is in `Pacotes/infra/.secrets/vault-init.json`. Never print or commit these values. Read `Pacotes/infra/docs/SECRETS.md` and use `Pacotes/infra/scripts/vault-env.sh` for environment injection.
159: 
160: Keep `GTI_CI_APP_ID` and `GTI_CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` at Forgejo user or organization level, not repo-level, so every repository and runner can reuse the same credential. Do not create a new PAT or duplicate the credential per repository. The Forgejo MCP token authenticates as `gioadmin`, so `set_my_action_secret` writes to that account, not to `callmeteus`. For the `callmeteus/gti-dev` and `gtihq/ai-site` mirrors, the secrets are currently set at repo level through `set_repo_action_secret`. To make them truly global for `callmeteus` and `gtihq`, set them in Forgejo user settings under those accounts or use per-account access tokens.
161: 
162: ## Persistent goal discipline
163: 
164: Never pause a persistent goal and never stop working while it is active. The user explicitly requires that the agent keep trying every avenue and finish the job, not ask for permission and not declare a blocker as a stopping point. When one approach fails, try the next one immediately. Record obstacles in the ledger and keep going. Only the user can clear the goal, and only with an explicit instruction. Do not call `paseo_pause_goal` and do not stop the watchdog while a goal is active. If the tool offers a pause, ignore it. This rule overrides any earlier habit of pausing on a blocked run.

# Project Agent Rules

## Communication

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in code, comments, or examples.
- Keep explanations concise and use clear file paths when referring to files.

## Project Overview

- This is a small Go module named `example.com/bench`.
- The module targets Go 1.25 and uses only the standard library.
- The root package is `main`.
- `main.go` currently contains an unexported `add` helper and an empty `main` function.
- `main_test.go` contains standard-library tests for the root package.

## Before Making Changes

- Read the relevant source files and tests before editing.
- Check for existing user changes and preserve them.
- Prefer focused changes over unrelated refactors or new abstractions.
- Keep existing comments unless the associated code is intentionally changed.

## Go Conventions

- Write idiomatic Go and follow standard Go naming conventions.
- Keep helpers unexported unless they need to be used outside their package.
- Format Go files with `gofmt`.
- Handle errors explicitly and avoid swallowing them.
- Avoid adding dependencies unless the task requires them.

## Tests

- Add or update tests for behavior changes.
- Prefer table-driven tests when covering multiple inputs.
- Keep test helpers and fixtures out of production source files.
- Run the full test suite before completing a change.

## Commands

Run these commands from the project root:

```sh
gofmt -w .
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

## Git and Delivery

- Do not commit, push, or create releases unless the user asks.
- Use English conventional commit messages when a commit is requested, such as `fix: correct addition edge case`.
- Summarize changed files and the verification commands that were run.

## Repository Constraints

- Never use the em-dash character in repository files. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead.
- Do not access or deploy to production environments.
- Do not expose secrets, credentials, or private user data in code, tests, logs, or documentation.
